source.title: Exploring Cross-model Neuronal Correlations in the Context of Predicting Model Performance and Generalizability
source.authors: Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie; Sajjad Ghiasvand; Lionel Levine; Majid Sarrafzadeh

record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-model representational alignment with a neuron-level best-match correlation metric, a different method from the cited representation-comparison approaches.
record.gate_note: The three tables report partial-correlation measurements between model pairs and are recorded below. Cited findings, proposed implications for accuracy or robustness, and unmeasured discussion claims are not rows. Measurements use only 10 ImageNet validation examples and one selected layer or stage per architecture family.
record.test_reason: The study measures neuron-level best-match correlation between ImageNet CNNs of different depths within three families. Its tables show how alignment changes with scale, which bears on V1's scale claim. It uses a different metric from the originals, and it does not compare across architectures, objectives or data.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that depth-adjacent variants align most, which they treat as validating the metric. They frame the score as a lightweight check of trustworthiness and compatibility. They do not frame it as evidence about convergence with scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses symmetric, absolute best-neuron Pearson correlations with a layer-distance penalty and partial layer matching; it does not use the cited methods as its measurement procedure.
record.problems: Only 10 ImageNet validation points are used, with one selected layer or stage per architecture family and partial matching rather than all-layer comparison. No uncertainty estimates or control comparisons are reported. Performance and capability are not measured alongside the correlation results.

untested.parts: Different architectures, objectives or data. Capability measured alongside alignment. Independent training is not established, since these are standard pretrained checkpoints.
Absolute incompleteness cannot be read without a chance baseline. Plateau and causes (shared data or objectives) are not tested.
The text claims stability across subsampling levels and layer choices but shows no numbers. No metric or input-distribution comparisons.

missing.what: An unquantified claim that partial-correlation values stay stable across subsampling levels and layer selection schemes. No numbers are shown.
A discussion claim, not measured, that shallower architectures show higher correlation with other networks.

record.verdict_notes: This is a weak test. It uses only 10 ImageNet images, one layer per family, no uncertainty and no chance baseline; best-match |r| over 10 samples is likely inflated by chance. All comparisons are within one family and use the same training data and objective. The ResNet decline may reflect the switch from basic to bottleneck blocks between ResNet-34 and ResNet-50, not scale. The method resembles Li et al.'s best-match neuron correlation, but it compares models of different depths rather than seeds, so V3 is not tested.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares differently scaled models within three architecture families, but does not test different objectives or modalities, independently trained model pairs, or whether alignment rises with measured capability or performance.
No paired image-caption or vision-language model comparisons.
No comparisons across random seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment evaluation.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
The study uses one similarity measure and a fixed probe set and selected layers; it does not compare metrics, settings, or input distributions.
The measurements show incomplete alignment in these model comparisons, but do not test whether shared training data or objectives cause it, or whether alignment plateaus generally.

rows.note: Pairwise alignment is measured, but the value alone does not establish a scale-related increase.
rows.check: This state is judged from the ResNet pattern, not the single pair. The smallest pair has the highest value (0.661), and alignment falls as both models grow, down to 101 vs 152 at 0.052. V7 link removed: there is no chance baseline, and best-match max-|r| over 10 probe images is inflated by chance, so absolute incompleteness cannot be read.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-18 to 152, fourth-layer output, 10 probe images
relationships.reason: Alignment falls as models grow: the smallest pair scores 0.661 (r01) and the largest 0.052 (r10), with r08 and r09 low too.
relationships.display_finding: Using 10 probe images, the smallest ResNet pair scores 0.661 alignment versus 0.052 for the largest pair.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: ImageNet ResNet-18 to 152, fourth-layer output, 10 probe images
source_check.reason: Table 1 shows an overall reversed scale pattern: 0.661 for ResNet-18/34 (r01), falling to 0.052 for ResNet-101/152 (r10), with low larger-model scores in r08–r09; the pattern is not strictly monotonic.

relationships.condition: DenseNet-121 to 201 and EfficientNet-B0 to B4, within family
relationships.reason: No rise with size: DenseNet is non-monotonic, 0.697–0.780 (r11–r16), and EfficientNet is flat, about 0.82 (r17–r26). The scale range is narrow and there are only 10 probes.
relationships.display_finding: Alignment varied non-monotonically from 0.697 to 0.780 for DenseNet and stayed around 0.82 for EfficientNet across 10 probes.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: DenseNet-121 to 201 and EfficientNet-B0 to B4, within family
source_check.reason: The stated finding is absence of the predicted scale increase: DenseNet is non-monotonic at 0.697–0.780 (r11–r16), and EfficientNet is approximately flat at 0.811–0.826 (r17–r24,r26). Under section 3, absence warrants challenges; narrow scale coverage and 10 probes are evidential limitations, not evidence of partial convergence with scale.

relation.reason: Its own pairwise alignment results bear on V1's scale prediction within the tested model families.

tranche.reason: The study measures representational alignment across model scales using a different neuron-level correlation method.

source_check.notes: Row states describe family-level scale patterns, not effects established by isolated pair scores. Only 10 probes and one selected layer or stage per family are tested; capability gains and convergence across different objectives or training datasets remain untested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Within-family ImageNet-pretrained ResNet, DenseNet, and EfficientNet comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The correlations do not show a consistent rise with model scale: ResNet values vary substantially, DenseNet values are non-monotonic, and EfficientNet values are similar across pairs (r01-r26).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: All reported within-family ImageNet-pretrained model pairs
reader_labels.reason: Every reported pair has a partial-correlation value below 1, indicating that measured alignment is not complete in these comparisons (r01-r26).
